principle: Every edge is derived from a recorded exchange and carries its evidence file. Nothing here is inferred from naming or convention.

nodes.gotcha: JSON key is businessUnitDescription. The 422 names DB column lngdsc and the recipe said description; BOTH are rejected. Only a UI network capture yields the real key.

The Add form is unusable. Carrier is a carrierLookup and Carrier Facility Address a wmAddress, both with EMPTY stores; even loading the store and setting the model value directly leaves the field reporting "This field is required". Save then fires nothing at all - no error, no modal, no request. Automation must bypass this form and POST directly. resourceId is {addressId}*!{carrier}*!{poolPointAddressId}.
Description key is longDescription, not description. API ships a typo: shotDescription (sic). csttyp truncates at 4 chars.

FOUR required fields, not two: vehicleTypeId, longDescription, voiceCode, vehicleLimit. voiceCode is NUMERIC, truncates to 2 chars, and must be UNIQUE across all equipment types - the form rejects a duplicate with "The voice code already existed", a second uniqueness constraint beyond the primary key. 77 types exist here; lowest free voiceCode was 11.

Collection is empty in this environment, so field names cannot be sampled from an existing record - driving the UI was the ONLY way to obtain this payload. The form label is "Name" (-> levelTypeName), not "Level Type". totalLevelUnits is required and loses its displayed default when the form re-renders.
locationTypeCategory (loc_typ_cat) is required and was undocumented
collection is NOT site-scoped; siteId/subsites cause a 500

hazards.impact: HIGH. The recipe told automation authors this screen was safe to retry. It leaks one address per failed attempt, exactly like clients. Recipe corrected.

The 'server-side vs client-side' split across the Partners screens was built partly on this. At the API layer a duplicate carrier does return 409 (http/exchanges/carriers.jsonl), but the UI never gets that far.

Stateful app-side behaviour: the same request transitioned from working to failing within one session. 'no rows affected' on an INSERT suggests the backend performs a lookup/update that now matches nothing. Not resolvable without backend visibility; recorded rather than guessed at.
hazards.operational_rule: DO NOT automate voice-device creation via this screen or via POST /wm/devices with deviceClass 'V'. Beyond the 404, a failed save WEDGES the screen permanently: the exception modal can be dismissed but its masks survive it, leaving the form unusable and poisoning any later step in the same session. Recovery requires removing .x-mask nodes from the DOM and changing route - see tools/cdp/recover.mjs. Treat this screen as manual-only until the backend behaviour is understood.
